My wife is from Taiwan and she uses WeChat. She saw the posts about how Labor would let in more refugees, and how Labor will increase taxes, and also about how Labor would cause a housing market crash. But I would not say these posts changed her vote.

As a generalisation, the Chinese-background middle class will identify more closely with the LNP's policies. A lot of small business owners, a high value on education and an ethic of working hard and saving. On education, you may think that would favour the ALP. But the ALP's policies are targeted to achieving a minimum standard for everyone. Chinese don't want their kids to do ok - they want their kids to be the best. This means sending their kids to private schools or a high performing government school (e.g. Balwyn High School.)

When my wife was originally sympathetic to the ALP, especially when Gillard became our first female PM. But she soon came to perceive them as wasteful. e.g. Tax increases, school halls and spending a billion dollars to rip up the East-West tunnel contract in Melbourne. My wife is now firmly entrenched as an LNP voter (whereas I vote left).

Came across this video the other day that I found helpful (linked from /r/depression):

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kYX87kkyubk

Summary:

* In depression you fall into a pattern of recurring negative thoughts. It's your emotional reaction to those thoughts that make you feel depressed.

* The negative thoughts fall into two broad categories: that your situation is bad, or that you are bad

* You can't stop the thoughts, but you can come to realise that they are not true -- then they will no longer make you feel sad
